rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 1 line 6, "One frontier skill already reached you as a plain prompt. The second-pass walk-down against your plan file, where Claude asked you one question at a time about unresolved branches, was patterned on Matt Pocock's `grill-me` skill" — this is chunk 1's own content, so there is no prior in-file slide to draw on, but the sentence is fully self-unpacking in the same breath (what happened + what it was patterned on), not a pronoun assuming outside memory — same shape as rule 2's own passing example. Second candidate: chunk 2 line 11 opens "Security practitioners. The two curated skills compress decades of judgement" before naming which two — resolved within the SAME bullet, two sentences later (STRIDE, then access-control) — cataphora inside one paragraph, not a deck-spanning forward reference. Confirmed the 2026-08-25/2026-08-29 cuts removing chunk 1's "Today the packaging arrives: you invoke two curated skills and author one of your own" left no orphaned forward pointer: chunk 4's header ("Two curated, one authored") and its own body still establish the ratio directly, in-chunk. Harm rule 1 guards against — a reader stuck on a referent with no way to resolve it — is not present anywhere in the current body.

Only cross-file callback in the current body: chunk 1 line 6 (quoted above) — names the source (Pocock's `grill-me`) and unpacks its claim in the same sentence rather than pointing at a file by position ("the earlier module said"), matching the rule's own stated passing shape. No other file-level callback exists in the body.

Z." construction anywhere — the only remaining single negations are line 21 "Your codebase is not a pyramid" and line 29 "None of them are compliance artifacts", each alone on its own bullet (the 2026-08-29 cut removed chunk 5's second negation, "Not 'we followed a checklist' but:", which had stacked two on one slide). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture headings should be claims per rule 15, but three remain noun-phrase/ratio labels with no verb/assertion: chunk 1 line 3 "What a skill is" (definitional label), chunk 2 line 9 "Borrowed judgement, or your own" (two-way label), chunk 4 line 19 "Two curated, one authored" (ratio label). None fits the stated NOT-violation carve-outs verbatim (orientation headers, catalogue entries naming their subject, phase/section labels inside a walk), though "Borrowed judgement, or your own" and "Two curated, one authored" read close to "catalogue entries naming their subject." By contrast chunk 3 ("Your authored skill starts personal, then compounds"), chunk 5 ("Three trust artifacts the next engineer checks"), and chunk 6 ("The tool flags; you make the call") are genuine subject+verb claims. Harm check, applying the template's own self-classifying principle for rules added after its blocking/non-blocking list was written: the failure mode here is register/mood, not comprehension — no reader is confused by "What a skill is", the slide's mood is simply a beat flatter than a declared law would be. That is "this could be tighter", not "I cannot follow this." This also matches the compendium's own documented history for this exact rule ("a rule that only ever produces notes is a rule mis-scoped") and Antti's own carve-out cited inside rule 15 itself ("not every header owes a claim"). Filed as a TODO, not a blocking finding.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If strict conformance is wanted: recast as claims, e.g. "A skill is judgement someone else already packaged" (ch1) / "Someone else's judgement, or yours" (ch2) / "Two proportions, and only one of them you can author" (ch4) — otherwise leave as labels; this rule's own history treats that as acceptable for a definitional/enumerating lecture slide.
